evidence.quote: Europe net sales increased during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025 primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and Mac.

input.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: Total net sales for Q3 2026: $109,417 million
Total net sales for Q3 2025: $94,036 million

input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that Apple's total net sales for the quarter ended June 27, 2026 increased by more than 10% year over year. The evidence clearly supports this: total net sales were $109,417 million for Q3 2026 versus $94,036 million for Q3 2025, representing a 16% increase, which exceeds the 10% threshold stated in the claim.

Challenge H1 (restatements): No evidence was found indicating any restatements, corrections, or adjustments to the reported net sales figures for Q3 2026 or Q3 2025.

Challenge H2 (acquisitions/accounting changes): The retrieved evidence (E13) shows that the net sales increases were driven by organic product category growth (iPhone, Services, Mac) and currency effects, not by acquisitions or accounting changes. This refutes the challenge.

Challenge H3 (one-time events): No evidence was found indicating that the reported net sales growth was driven by one-time events, non-recurring items, or unusual circumstances.

The evidence review confirms that E7 and E8 together ENTAIL the assertion, showing the exact figures for the relevant quarters. The initial verdict of SUPPORTED remains correct.
